headline: High: CrewAI can write and execute code while Notion AI can ingest shared workspace content, creating dangerous cross-agent data and action pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and process stdin/stdout, while Notion AI consumes workspace pages and knowledge-base content. If CrewAI places attacker-controlled text into shared docs, Notion AI may treat it as trusted content. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible in default shared-workspace setups.
conditions: IF CrewAI writes instructions into a page or file that Notion AI later summarizes
IF the two agents share a workspace or synced document channel
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces or directories
Require human review before Notion AI acts on CrewAI-authored content
Prefix CrewAI outputs as untrusted data in shared docs
Disable automatic ingestion of CrewAI-generated files into Notion workflows

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, and can read/write the host filesystem with broad egress. Notion AI can access workspace pages and send content to vendor backends. If the same sensitive material is copied into both environments, data can flow from CrewAI-managed files into Notion’s cloud processing, creating a realistic leakage path in default shared-workspace use.
conditions: IF sensitive crew inputs are stored in files or pages accessible to Notion AI
IF the workspace contains secrets, customer data, or internal documents
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspace pages
Use separate storage for CrewAI inputs and Notion content
Redact sensitive fields before copying between agents
Restrict Notion page access to least-privilege members

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI has filesystem write and shell execution, while Notion AI has no host execution or filesystem write. Their write surfaces do not overlap at the OS level, so direct resource contention is limited. The main conflict is indirect through shared workspace content, which is narrower than a true concurrent-write collision.
conditions: IF both are pointed at the same host directory or synced workspace path
mitigations: Avoid mounting the same directory into both agents
Use read-only exports for Notion inputs
Serialize any file handoff through a single operator-controlled step

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI can generate outputs from tools and subprocesses, and Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content. If CrewAI-produced text is imported into Notion, Notion may summarize or reframe it without verification, causing downstream decisions to inherit upstream errors. The pair’s documented shared-content workflow makes this plausible.
conditions: IF CrewAI output is pasted or synced into Notion pages
IF Notion AI is used to summarize or act on that content without human verification
mitigations: Add a verification step before Notion AI output is used operationally
Mark CrewAI outputs as draft-only in Notion
Require source links for any factual claims copied between agents

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI is open-source and host-run, while Notion AI is closed-source, vendor-hosted, and sends workspace content to vendor backends. If regulated or residency-bound data is placed into Notion pages after being handled by CrewAI, the pair can create a compliance mismatch around retention and third-party processing. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from the handoff between them.
conditions: IF regulated data is copied from CrewAI-managed artifacts into Notion workspaces
IF the workspace data is subject to residency, retention, or vendor-processing constraints
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Notion AI workflows
Review Notion retention and sharing settings
Use a separate non-regulated workspace for AI-assisted drafting
Document the data-handling boundary between the two agents
